key_insight: A privacy-preserving local hybrid system using a small language model plus rules can accurately extract uncoded urinary tract infection features from multilingual primary-care EHR free text.
clinical_relevance: This could help convert narrative notes into structured data for research, quality improvement, and risk stratification without sending sensitive records to external cloud LLMs.
method: Ran Phi4-mini (3.8B) locally inside the institutional firewall with Ollama.
Combined clinician-refined prompts with deterministic regular expressions to extract six UTI features.
Validated against a double-blind clinician gold standard and an adversarial synthetic noise dataset.
evidence_signal: On 15,498 EHR narratives from 2,962 patients, the pipeline identified 4,663 feature occurrences and achieved 93.8% accuracy in real-world clinician validation, with 83.6% sensitivity and 96.6% specificity.
watch_item: Performance was validated on a focused UTI feature set, so broader deployment may require retraining, local language adaptation, and monitoring for edge cases or site-specific documentation styles.
paper_title: Uncoded Clinical Features from Multilingual Electronic Health Records in Catalonia: Development and Validation Study
